root_cause: Two causes, not one. (a) dawn_valley: the volumetric fog lights every column with the horizon ring's colour for its azimuth (psFogInject g_air). The ring samples the sky from 2 degrees above the land, which toward a low sun is the aureole's flank (4 to 9 degrees from the sun in dawn_valley). The haze over the bay looks 15 to 20 degrees away from the sun but took that light anyway. The haze converges to it, so the bay and shore sank into a cream column. Probes: fogDensity=0 makes the bay crisp (bay std 57.1, mean 98) against base (32.8, 154). With the fix but the ring's elevation row ignored (shots_p2), the bay mean is 134 against 128, so the measured elevation matters. (b) sunrise_ridge is not the fog: fogDensity=0 leaves the dome unchanged. camSkyLook turns a low sun's sky toward the zenith blue only "away from the sun's glow", masked by the plain angle to the sun (none within 10 degrees, all from 30 degrees). That mask is a disc, so the golden colour filled a disc of about 20 degrees radius round a 5 degree sun. Warmth (R-B) was 82 at 200 px up and 47 at 300 px up, against 77 at 400 px and 51 at 600 px to the side.
change_summary: (a) psFogRing now writes a second row holding the sine of the mean elevation of the samples it kept, blended over frames like the colour. The ring target is kFogRingBins x 2. For each of its 9 ring taps, psFogInject builds the tap's real direction. A new fogSkyParts reads the sky table's two parts there: r is Rayleigh plus multiple scattering, m is the haze's single scattering without phase. Each tap then gets a per-channel gain (r + m P(column)) / (r + m P(tap)), where P is the sky's own skyMiePhase, clamped to 0..kFogRingPhaseMax. The gain needs the sky table on (litAtmo.z), fades out under a grey sky (fogWeather.z) and is off at night. A column that looks where the ring measured keeps the ring colour, so far ground still melts into the sky behind it. Results: bay std/mean 32.8/154 to 37.7/128, far shore 13.8/172 to 16.4/147. There is a C++ mirror, FogRingPhaseGain. (b) The camSkyLook mask uses a new camLowSunGlowCos. It counts height above the sun 3 times (kLowSunGlowFlat) and treats sky below the sun's height as at the sun's height (C++ mirror PhotoCamera LowSunGlowCos). The warm glow becomes a band hugging the horizon, brightest near the sun: warmth 41 at 200 px up and 1 at 300 px up, against 74 and 49 to the side. Check views: lowsun_fp and coastline_sunset improved (the glow is a band, the land under the sun is crisper); forest_edge_golden is unchanged. Meter untouched.
remaining: dawn_valley is still hazier than landed on the sun side (bay std 37.7 against 53.3). What remains is the sky part of the air's light plus the haze's thickness, a density question. In sunrise_ridge the warm hue is now a band, but a pale bright aureole disc round the sun remains (luminance, from the sky table under the roll-off). The forward lobe (kFogLobeGain 0.2) now sits on light that already carries the phase per column and could be lowered later. Only the five views were shot, at 1080; the 960x640 cuts and the night and grey views were not reshot (the ring gain is off at night and fades out under grey skies). The shots were taken before a comment-only header edit; the final build (exit 0) has the same code. root_cause:
The camera meter read the sun's deliberate burn. In round 4 the sky's roll-off cap toward the sun went from kSkyRolloffCap 2.4 up to kSkySunCap 10 (camSkyRolloff(lin, d)). The meter pass reads the stored frame, so sky taps within a few degrees of the sun read several times brighter: the cap is still 3.0 at 4 degrees and 2.7 at 6. Three guards in TargetExposureLog2 read those taps and stopped the camera down: the highlight percentile, SkyTopPeak and SunRingPeak. Those guards were tuned on the plain cap.

Probe 0 added the guards' readings to the readout and replayed the guards step by step on the base build. On woods_pine2_evening the meter's mean alone asks for 3.38. The highlight guard takes it to 2.44, the sky-top guard to 1.44 and the ring guard to 0.24, matching the logged ev 0.27 and frame mean 35. The meter mean was unchanged.

Probe 1 set kCamSkySunCap back to 2.4 with a shader override. It brought back most of the loss in every sun view: woods 1.43, lowsun_fp -0.15, sinai_lowsun_fp 0.57, dawn_valley 0.03. Also setting fogSun 0.4 (the beam gain back at round 3's 14) adds another 0.1 to 0.25 EV.
change_summary:
The fix is in the meter; the render keeps its burn. In the meter pass, each sky tap first goes through meterSkyLight. That function undoes the roll-off toward the sun along the tap's own view ray, then re-applies the plain-cap roll-off. The result is that the mean, the block peaks and the sky peaks all read the sky round the sun as round 3's meter did. Far from the sun and under the knee it is the identity. The disc and anything past the sun cap read as the plain cap.

- EngineGL33_Camera.cpp PostCameraMeter: sets those uniforms from PhotoCamera.hpp's own constants (no copied numbers in GLSL) and the sun's view-space direction from the camera.
- PhotoCamera.hpp/.cpp: new SkyMeterLight, the C++ mirror used by the tests.
- FeatureGates.hpp/.cpp and CameraReadoutNow: the readout now ends with "skytop= ring= ringw= free=", appended after skip=, so a capture log shows which guard holds a frame down.

root_cause: The round-4 tests for the AI fog link only exercised the pure helpers. Case 421 called UpdateFogSightMedium directly. That function never receives gate state, so the case could not fail, and nothing drove SimulateFogSight, which is the call the engine makes. I proved this with a mutation: I made SimulateFogSight drop AI sight when post effects are off. The old case still passed (8 assertions) and the new [aisight] cases failed (8 assertions in 2 cases). I reverted the mutation and rebuilt clean. The probe also turned up a second bug: in classic lighting the published drawn medium kept the last remastered frame's values (probe_1: classic state drawn=1, Tdrawn 0.9981 against Tai 0.9962). EngineGL33::UpdateFogMedium publishes it only on the remastered path, and the classic early return in UploadLitFrameConstants never cleared it. AI never reads it, so only probes and the drift guard were misled. Thread safety: FogSightMedium() returned a reference into static state that the next step rewrites.
change_summary: 1) New tests/unit/engine/Poseidon/World/test_fog_sight_link.cpp, tag [aisight], registered in tests/unit/engine/Poseidon/CMakeLists.txt. It drives Poseidon::SimulateFogSight on a real Landscape (a valley, setFog 0.3) with an EngineDummy subclass that reports each render-path state: post effects off, classic lighting, volFog off, fog quality knobs, all gates off with an interior view, another or no drawn medium, a 300 m view distance, and no renderer. AI medium and transmittance must stay bit-identical. It also checks: AI air equals the renderer's recipe (WorldFogInputs + aridity, ComputeFogMedium(in, tuning, true)) across fogDensity x fogMist; determinism (a cold-start client with no renderer gives an identical map and T, rebuilt only when the ground changes, and a copied medium does not follow the next step); per-machine inputs never reach AI's terms; and a source contract over all engine/ sources (only VolumetricFog.* and TerrainLighting.* may set AI sight, only WorldSetup.cpp calls SimulateFogSight, it runs after the sun, weather and SetFog and before PerformAI, Target.cpp multiplies by FogSightTransmittance, and the renderer takes WorldFogInputs and AI's map). The old case 421 now has a comment pointing to [aisight]. 2) FogSightMedium() returns by value, and the header documents the main-thread contract, with a static_assert. 3) EngineGL33_Lighting.cpp: the classic branch of UploadLitFrameConstants calls SetDrawnFogMedium(nullptr). 4) New probe verb triAiSight [observer, target], which returns the real EntityAI::CalcVisibility next to classic, size, Tai and Tdrawn. The in-game probe at the optics staging (fog 0.3) shows fogAi = Tai on every line, and Tai = Tdrawn on all 7 drawn lines (valley floor 0.9293 at 255 m). With post effects off or in classic lighting, AI is unchanged and drawn=0. 5) The optional ground field ready at load was not done (needs a new Engine API; design in NOTES.txt).

root_cause:
Object::DrawDecal lit every lit particle (smoke, dust, a fireball's soot) with the classic sun: sun->FullResult(0.5), which is 0.375 x LightSun::Diffuse plus the full Ambient, times the 1.6 accommodation. Under the photoreal camera, pre-lit draws are stored without pre-exposure, so a puff showed the classic light's colour and level while the world around it is lit by the rig and white-balanced to the rig's illuminant.

A probe log in UploadLitFrameConstants (removed before the patch) showed that at firefight_3 (sun -1.73 deg) the classic sun diffuse is still a red-pink sunset sun, (0.639, 0.240, 0.184). The classic model keeps it shining until 5 deg under the horizon. The rig's sun is 0 and its sky fill is a dim blue-grey that the camera balances to white. The puff light was therefore (0.43, 0.19, 0.17), salmon, and the white balance pushed it further toward pink.

An A/B in one build (a probe switch forcing the classic path, same pinned staging) gave a classic-lit middle foot of (89.5, 54.0, 50.5) over the sky's (82.6, 55.1, 49.5), and a rig-lit foot of (57.4, 41.8, 41.3). By day the same path clipped smoke to a blue-white column.
change_summary:
Lit particles now take the photoreal rig's light instead of the classic sun.
- LightRig: new function ParticleRigIrradiance. It gives a puff kParticleKeyShare of the key light (the sun dimmed by the cloud field's mean, or the moon under the moon key) and of the moon's shadowless rest. It adds the sky's irradiance averaged over all directions (zenith, both horizon sides and the ground bounce, 0.25 each), times the world's SurfaceShadeFactor.
- EngineGL33 UploadLitFrameConstants: stores that light times the rig's exposure (with the burst flash gain) and the frame's pre-exposure, which is how the world passes store scene light. The new Engine virtual ParticleRigLight hands it out for the current frame only.
- Object::DrawDecal: under the camera it drops the classic sun term and adds the rig light, at the material brightness, in linear light. Local lamps, physical night lights, combat lights and the fireball glow are unchanged.
- Firefight timing (b): abel_lighting.test.sqf view 7, both halves, now steps a fixed 1/30 s from the first shell to the third shot (new capFixStep, logged as event=fixstep), then returns to real time. Camera and staging are unchanged.

root_cause: (b) Specks: in an optic-overlay frame the fog apply puts the overlay's darkening back per channel as clamp(over / max(lin0, 1e-5)). Where the overlay did not draw, over and lin0 are both RGBA8 resolves of the same frame, so they are equal. But a world channel at code 0 decodes to 0, which gives a ratio of 0, and code 1 decodes to 5e-6, under the 1e-5 floor, which gives 0.5. Dark pine needles at code 0 or 1 therefore came out as black specks, or green ones when only G was above 1. TAA's LOD bias makes more of those dark texels, which is why taa=0 hid most of them. Probes: knob runs (the sight view has TAA off and still shows specks), a raw current-frame TAA override (the specks are already in the composite), and a fog-apply marker override (snapshot frames, specks inside clusters of near-black pixels). (a) and (c): on grey days the highlight guard held the frame's bright end, which is the mist or the deck, at 1.3 scene light, deep in the curve's shoulder (ev 1.04, high -0.58). The day setFog medium also stacked weather fog, the clear haze, humid air and valley mist. The rain streaks were cut to 0.45 and TAA averaged away what was left.

The speck counter goes from 39 green and 16 dark to 0 and 0. Grey-day camera: by day the highlight limit moves toward kGreyHighlightLimit 0.8 as the weather veil rises; TargetExposureLog2 has a new veil argument and the camera stores the veil each frame. Day setFog is thinner: kSetFogBoost 0.75 to 0.3 (the night is kept by kNightFogBoost 17.67), kMistFogWeight 0.6 to 0.2, and a new kSetFogHazeCut 0.5 cuts the clear haze under a day's setFog. Under rain the grey deck darkens by 1 - 0.4 x rain (kDeckRainDark, read from litWeather.y), and the streak share goes 0.45 to 0.9.
